blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
The employer brand of a modern company is shaped by countless signals the company barely controls: Glassdoor reviews, LinkedIn posts from former employees, leaked internal memos, interview experiences shared on Reddit and, increasingly, the public positions the company takes on contested social issues. That reality has forced a redefinition of what employer branding actually is. It cannot, realistically, be a carefully curated story delivered through owned channels; it has to be managed as reputation — an ongoing dialogue in which authenticity is the only defensible strategy.

The moment the internal reality and the external story diverge, the market notices within weeks. For HR leaders, this creates an uncomfortable but necessary alliance with communications, legal and the executive office. A bad first-month experience for a new hire is no longer only an HR problem; it is a reputation risk.

Conversely, a strong, honest culture is perhaps the most durable competitive moat a company can build. No marketing campaign outlives an uncomfortable internal truth, and former employees remain the most credible narrators of what a company is really like to work for.

items.q: According to the text, what shapes a modern employer brand?
options: Carefully curated stories on owned channels
Countless signals the company barely controls
items.why: "signals the company barely controls: Glassdoor reviews… leaked internal memos…".

items.q: According to the text, employer branding now has to be managed as…
items.why: "it has to be managed as reputation — an ongoing dialogue in which authenticity is the only defensible strategy."

items.q: What happens when internal reality and the external story diverge?
options: Only the legal team is affected
items.why: "The moment the internal reality and the external story diverge, the market notices within weeks."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A polished campaign can compensate for a poor internal culture.
A strong culture is a durable competitive advantage.
Former employees influence how a company is perceived.
A bad onboarding experience is a reputational matter.
items.why: Inferência: "No marketing campaign outlives an uncomfortable internal truth" — a campanha não compensa a cultura ruim.

items.q: The description of former employees as "the most credible narrators" suggests that…
options: the company's own messaging carries less trust than ex-staff accounts
only current staff should speak about the culture
narration is a formal HR function
items.why: Inferência: se os ex-funcionários são os mais críveis, a comunicação oficial da empresa pesa menos na percepção.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily coordenando a resposta a uma crise reputacional. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thanks for jumping on this at short notice. By now you've all seen the article — a former colleague, published this morning, and it's already circulating on LinkedIn. So let me set out where I think we stand.

My instinct is that we do not go into denial mode. Half of what he describes is, frankly, accurate — the onboarding was a mess last year, and pretending otherwise will only hand him a second story. Legal, I hear you on exposure, but a defensive statement that everyone can see is untrue does more damage than the piece itself.

What I'd propose is this: we acknowledge the specific failures that are real, we say plainly what we've changed since, and we resist the urge to relitigate his personal grievances in public. Communications, that means a short, human note — no corporate boilerplate.

And internally, before any of that goes out, I want our own people to hear it from us first. If the staff read our response on Reddit before their inbox, we've lost them too. Let's align on the wording by four, and we hold the line together — no freelancing to journalists.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What is Emily's overall instinct about how to respond?
options: Not to go into denial mode and to acknowledge what is true
To deny everything the article claims
items.why: "My instinct is that we do not go into denial mode… Half of what he describes is, frankly, accurate."

items.q: Why does Emily push back on a purely defensive statement?
options: The board has not approved it
It would take too long to draft
A statement everyone can see is untrue does more damage than the article
items.why: "a defensive statement that everyone can see is untrue does more damage than the piece itself."

items.q: What does Emily want Communications to produce?
options: A rebuttal of every point in the article
A short, human note with no boilerplate
items.why: "a short, human note — no corporate boilerplate."

items.q: When Emily says "pretending otherwise will only hand him a second story," she implies that…
options: the story should be handed to another journalist
the company should tell a different story
denying accurate claims would give the critic fresh ammunition
the employee is writing a sequel
items.why: Inferência: negar o que é verdade cria um novo escândalo (a mentira), reforçando o crítico.

items.q: Why does Emily insist staff hear the response first?
options: Journalists will not cover it otherwise
If employees learn of it externally, the company loses their trust too
The response is only for internal use
items.why: Inferência: "If the staff read our response on Reddit before their inbox, we've lost them too" — perder a confiança interna agrava a crise.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "A strong culture is the most durable competitive moat a company can build." A competitive moat is…
options: a lasting advantage rivals struggle to copy
items.why: Competitive moat = barreira competitiva: uma vantagem difícil de replicar.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The moment the internal reality and the external message ___, journalists start asking questions."
items.why: To diverge = divergir, separar-se — quando a realidade e a mensagem deixam de coincidir.

items.q: "HR can no longer curate the story on its own terms." To curate here means to…
options: carefully select and shape what is shown
items.why: To curate = curar/selecionar: montar deliberadamente a narrativa exibida.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The board treated the poor onboarding not as a minor HR issue but as a genuine ___."
items.why: Reputational risk = risco reputacional: algo que ameaça a imagem pública da empresa.

items.q: Owned channels are best described as…
options: media the company itself controls, like its careers page
items.why: Owned channel = canal próprio: mídia que a própria empresa controla e publica.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem na gestão de reputação e comunicação. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Legal still has to sign off on the public statement." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We need to get ahead of the story before it spreads further." To get ahead of means to…
options: ignore it and hope it fades
items.why: Get ahead of = antecipar-se, agir antes que a situação escape do controle.

items.q: "The article gained traction on LinkedIn within hours." This means it…
options: was paid for by the company
items.why: Gain traction = ganhar tração, começar a repercutir e a circular.

items.q: "Once the crisis passes, the accusations will blow over." To blow over means to…
options: fade and stop being a problem
items.why: Blow over = passar, arrefecer — a tempestade se dissipa.

items.q: "The whole leadership team needs to close ranks and speak with one voice." To close ranks means to…
options: unite and present a united front
items.why: Close ranks = fechar fileiras: unir-se e agir de forma coesa diante de uma ameaça.
